(i) the composition of Kv1 channel subunits in the brain is heterogeneous; (ii) this heterogeneity is reflected in the competitive behaviour of toxins for binding in brain; (iii) the composition of the toxin binding site is not uniform throughout the brain.

alpha-dendro toxin and kaliotoxin have the same affinity for binding to the same sites in the brain, but the affinity of mast cell degranulation peptide for binding to these sites is different.

the development of new tools for the analysis of Kv1 channels in brain.
the development of novel drugs that target specific neuronal channels and receptors.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of multiple toxins to label Kv1 channels in the brain provides an effective way to identify the different types of Kv1 channel in different brain structures.
the use of a single toxin to label brain structures is likely to lead to a significant underestimation of Kv1 channel diversity.
autoradiographic competition analysis can provide information about the composition of the channels that are labelled in a given region of brain.
